ConnectionStrings.//Postgres: Real value is provided via .NET user-secrets (no secret in the repo — Art. VI.4 / ADR-0012).

//Demo: E3-06 review data. When 'Demo:Seed' is true, a hosted seeder creates the 2026-2027 schooljaar, one klas and a voorgesteld jaarplan on startup IF that school year does not already exist — so the kalender shows something honest at the directie/teacher review without needing an Azure AI call first. It is DELIBERATELY NOT SET HERE. WebApplicationFactory loads this file, so a value here runs the seeder inside every integration test: it did, and it broke SchoolcontentBeheerEndpointsTests by colliding on the thema 'Water'. The flag lives in Properties/launchSettings.json instead — 'a developer started this by hand', which is never loaded by a test host. To seed against some other environment, pass Demo__Seed=true explicitly.
//KeyVault: Cloud only (E0-07 / ADR-0012). Set 'KeyVault:Uri' (or env KeyVault__Uri) to a vault URI in non-Development environments to bind Azure Key Vault as a config source. Absent locally → no-op (no Azure dependency). NEVER commit a real vault URI or secret (Art. VI.4).
//AzureAI: AI keys are SERVER-SIDE ONLY (Art. VI.4 / Art. IV). The Azure AI Foundry client exists as of E2-01 (Infrastructure, bound from the 'AzureAI' section). Non-secret values ('AzureAI:Endpoint', 'AzureAI:Deployment', 'AzureAI:ApiVersion') may live here per environment; the SECRET 'AzureAI:ApiKey' lives in user-secrets locally / Key Vault in the cloud — never in the repo, never exposed to the frontend. Local command: dotnet user-secrets set "AzureAI:ApiKey" "<your-foundry-key>" --project src/Jaarplanner.Api
